title: How Shall My Inward Joys Arise
description: How Shall My Inward Joys Arise in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 39, headed “God's tender care of his church, Isa. 13 &c”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How shall my in-ward joys a-rise And burst in-to a song, Al-might-y love in-spires my heart, And plea-sure tunes my tongue.

lines: How shall my inward joys arise
And solemn oaths have bound his love
Why do we then indulge our fears,
Is he a God, and shall his grace
Can a kind woman e'er forget
"Deep on the palms of both my hands
"My hands shall raise her ruin'd walls,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
